solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pole a close friend

definitions.meaning: a stout pole, as used for a ship's mast or boom
a dialect word (Liverpool and elsewhere) for a mate or best pal

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a rounded timber pole on a ship, and a regional word for a pal.

clue.text: Dads love no-good chart hit?

parts.note: pops is an informal word for fathers
love is zero in tennis, a nought shaped like O
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Fathers who adore some worthless song topping the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that climbs the hit parade is typically a commercial chart-pop number; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Pick up exchange in court

definitions.meaning: to recover or improve, as markets or a patient may
a long sequence of shots between players on a tennis court

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to recover strength, and a back-and-forth series of strokes in tennis or squash.

clue.text: Thrill to support illegal payment

parts.note: a kick is a buzz or thrill
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Getting a buzz from endorsing a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe paid secretly in return for a contract or favour is a well-known synonym.

clue.text: King has very little money to drop off

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
one penny, written 1p, read as I and P

explanation.surface: A monarch who is nearly broke has to sleep it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little money' is 1p, a single British penny, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word meaning to sleep, so to doze off is the same verb sense.

clue.text: Lots tucking into fish and a fizzy drink

indicators.note: the word for lots goes inside the fish, as food is tucked into

parts.note: a cod is a fish
reams means a great quantity, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: Loads of something being eaten with fish and a sparkling beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet carbonated soft drink flavoured with vanilla, a straightforward example.

clue.text: Variety of tree bug that's swollen by drink?

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A kind of insect living in trees has become bloated from drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built up by heavy ale consumption is a belly enlarged by alcohol, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: What can symbolise, say, one family or a hundred others

definitions.text: What can symbolise, say, one family

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A riddle about an emblem representing one household or a hundred others.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic emblem above a shield is a badge that stands for a family line.

clue.text: Perfect order for dessert

definitions.meaning: ... order is an idiom for complete neatness
a baked fruit pudding with pastry

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for immaculate tidiness, and the pastry pudding served after a meal.

clue.text: Quits flat

definitions.meaning: being quits means having settled up, owing nothing either way
level or smooth, with no bumps

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: square with someone after a debt is settled, and level in surface.

clue.text: Some onyx offered in return? Cunning!

indicators.note: in return means the picked letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run spanning both

explanation.surface: Someone offered a gemstone in exchange, a crafty move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes YXOF from 'onyx offered'; 'in return' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly and crafty, like the fox of fable, so an adjective synonym for shrewd guile.

clue.text: Huge myth Gail propagated

indicators.note: propagated suggests spreading and reproducing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legend about someone called Gail spread widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally used to mean enormous or tremendous, as in an almighty row.

clue.text: What can fly inside adrenal pore after rising

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
inside says the letters sit within these clue words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A medical riddle about something airborne within a gland's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'inside' in the definition, leaving the hidden step with no signal; 'inside' is that indicator. 'inside' takes ENALPOREA from the clue words and 'rising' (a down clue) reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered aircraft with fixed wings is a thing that flies, a broad definition by description.

clue.text: More revolting gruel I spilled

indicators.note: spilled suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A disgusting porridge that someone knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word for ugly, nasty, so more unpleasant or repulsive.

clue.text: Stop in furniture store to see decorative art

indicators.note: in places the word for stop inside the store name

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain
to ban something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Popping into a furniture shop to look at ornamental art.
explanation.walkthrough: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain; 'to see' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of flower arrangement is an ornamental art form.

clue.text: Blooming bishop I had to defeat at auction?

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A flourishing clergyman admitting he beat rivals at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer more money than a rival bidder, beating them in a sale.

clue.text: Shunned US serviceman, on reflection, not a communist!

indicators.note: on reflection means the letters are mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
no can mean not, as in no better
red is a familiar term for a communist

explanation.surface: An American soldier, thinking it over, was snubbed for not being a leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cold-shouldered means being deliberately paid no attention, a synonym in past tense.

clue.text: Climber having dessert in front of mountain top, briefly

indicators.note: in front of places the dessert word before the next piece

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding course

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A mountaineer eating pudding just short of the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant flowering plant that clambers up supports, so a climbing plant.

clue.text: Silver currently is returned for money

indicators.note: returned means the combined letters come back the other way

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
now means at present

explanation.surface: Silver at present comes back as cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses AGNOW. Wonga is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cash, so a direct informal synonym.

clue.text: Sea eagle to bring home, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: to earn is to bring home pay

explanation.surface: A seabird of prey being taken home, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed coastal bird of prey, a crossword stalwart.

clue.text: Girl's Spanish article including English translation

indicators.note: including means the article holds the other piece inside

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
the English rendering of el is the

explanation.surface: A girl's Spanish essay that includes an English version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' is not an anagram signal: the English translation of the Spanish article is the English article.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Girl acting naturally, not artificially, at first

indicators.note: at first means taking the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A girl performing without pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Everyone in attendance? Sound!

parts.note: all means everyone
someone in attendance is present, at the place in question

explanation.surface: A roll call asking whether everybody is present, answered with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like a definition of a whole group present, but it is two pieces building the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being mentally sound, of sane and alert mind.

clue.text: Note young prince brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read bottom to top

parts.note: Hal is Prince Henry as a youth in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: A message about a prince who was raised.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth sol-fa syllable, a musical note.

clue.text: He tangled with Tarzan in ME town

definitions.note: ME stands for the Middle East

indicators.note: tangled means the letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fought with Tarzan in a Middle Eastern town.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's hometown in Galilee, a settlement in the Middle East.

clue.text: Boy with yen to find female

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A lad with a craving goes looking for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' also means a longing, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite word for a woman, a straightforward synonym.
